analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The visible hunks are documentation: a 15-second per-model unload timeout on shutdown after drain, and `status` text about config changes needing a restart (`enabled_models_at_start`, `enabled_models_at_last_switch` in the daemon state). The supplied units are base_text excerpts (lines 1290-2036) from other regions of the file, so the changed lines themselves are only visible in the truncated patch excerpt. I could not cite any head line, and the excerpt may omit parts of the change.

I checked the unchanged base text against the threat model: provider token handling (A-008), add-on hold socket files (TB-012, T-059), the prefix-cache SSD tier (T-041), the fan helper (TB-010), and the attestation and App Attest passthrough. The documented behavior matches the model, and this PR modifies none of it.

For the shutdown change, a model whose native retirement never finishes is left to process exit. That is an availability and cleanup-ordering behavior. If it leaves GPU memory or KV state uncleared until exit, T-028 residual-data and T-029 apply, but process exit clears that memory. I found no security regression in the docs.

Remaining integration questions: whether the code behind `ProviderLoop.unloadAllModelsForShutdown` matches the docs, and whether the new daemon-state fields expose sensitive data. Both are outside the supplied evidence.
